verdict.printed: Page 38 has the title 覆盆子 (Raspberry), an illustration of a thorny raspberry plant, and the running header 三才圖會卷之草木十一 with page number 二十. It has no body text.
verdict.evidence: The English body, "Chestnuts are found everywhere... Hanyang and Fanyang... chestnut wedge... benefit the vital energy", renders the chestnut entry printed on page 37. Page 38 prints only the header, the page number and the title "Raspberry". The header and title are rendered, but the body text is not from page 38.

verdict.printed: Page 32 is nearly blank. It has only the short title 備東說 (On Defending the East) at the top right, plus faint, illegible margin text.
verdict.evidence: The English body, from "The Taiyi Spirit… is in the Fourth Palace" through "The First Strike Spirit approaches Lüshen", renders page 31 (太乙在四宮 … 始擊臨呂申). Only the heading "On Defending the East" is page 32's own text. The English also adds a volume number, 'Page 15', and glosses such as 'A numerical value derived from the Taiyi cycle'.

verdict.printed: Page 18 has an illustration of the 萬年青 plant, with the caption 萬年青 and the volume marker 木類卷之三十八. It has no body text.
verdict.evidence: "According to the Relief Herbal, the Jili Nut Tree is also known as the Jimizhi..." is the 吉利子樹 entry printed on page 17. Only the header lines ("Woody Plants, Volume 38" and "Evergreen") come from page 18. The gloss on chi is a minor addition.

verdict.printed: Page 177 prints only the title '搜神記卷七' (Soushenji, Volume 7) in a ruled-column frame, with the running header 欽定四庫全書 and 卷七 in the margin.
verdict.evidence: The heading 'In Search of the Supernatural, Volume 7' renders page 177's own title. The body ('Previously, those who made handles for feather fans...', 'Wang Dun's southern campaign', 'large snake in Wuchang') renders page 176's text. The bracketed '[323 AD]' and the 'bǐng' gloss are added, and the final note about the text cutting off is also not printed on the page.

verdict.printed: Page 79 has only the title 五星聚奎璧 (Five Stars Gather at Kui) above a faded illustration of figures. It has no body text.
verdict.evidence: The body "Confucius once said: 'I have heard that when the Emperor Yao led Shun...' five elders... River Map" translates the 五老告河圖 text printed on page 78. Page 79's own title is rendered only as the heading "Five Stars Gathering in the Kui Mansion".

verdict.printed: Page 39 has only the title 黑疔瘡圖 (Illustration of the Black Furuncle) above a woodcut of a bearded, capped man seated on a stool.
verdict.evidence: The body renders page 38's White Furuncle text: "White Furuncles are caused by deficiency-heat in the large intestine... use Needle-tip Powder". Only the final heading "Illustration of the Black Furuncle" and the picture description belong to page 39. The English also adds glosses such as the Frankincense and Astragalus Powder explanation.

verdict.printed: Page 52 has only the title 水塘圖 and a woodblock picture of a pond with lotus, reeds, willows and hills. It has no body text.
verdict.evidence: "The Dictionary of Word Explanations says that a reservoir is a wilderness pond..." and the list of Lujiang, Yingchuan and Huangling ponds render page 51's text (說文曰陂野池也... 芍陂, 鴻隙陂). Only "Illustration of a Water Pond" is on page 52.

verdict.printed: Page 73 prints only the title 懸燈製 and a drawing of a lantern hung from a bracket on a wall. It has no body text.
verdict.evidence: "[The lamps should be suspended] seven feet off the ground... the enemy cannot use the ropes to climb" renders page 72's text, which starts 離地七尺庶使賊抵城下. Page 73 does not print this. The English also adds glosses for terms such as liao jiakou, xuansuo, panji, duo and huoqiu. The title "Design of Hanging Lamps" is rendered, so own_text is partly.

verdict.printed: Page 27 is an illustration of the Yuanzhi plant. It carries the running title 植物名實圖考, the plant name 遠志, the page number 十三 and 山草卷之七. There is no body text.
verdict.evidence: The title, "Mountain Herbs, Volume 7", "Page 13" and the heading "Yuanzhi" are rendered from page 27's own printed text. The body paragraphs, such as "Yuanzhi is listed as a 'superior grade' herb in the Classic of the Roots and Herbs" and "The Illustrated Classic records several varieties", translate the page 26 text (遠志本經上品…圖經載數種). There is also some added commentary on top of that translation.

verdict.printed: Page 23 has only the running header (芥子園畫傳 卷三) and the picture caption 又主山自為環抱法 beside a mountain landscape. It has no body text.
verdict.evidence: The body, "The previous illustration relied on the 'Guest Peaks'... Great Sovereign presiding over the Bright Hall", translates the paragraph printed on page 22 (前圖藉客峰以成氣象…大君臨明堂). Page 23 prints only the caption, which the English heading "Another Method: The Main Mountain Enclosing Itself" does render.

verdict.printed: Cover with the title 增廣本草綱目 in a framed label, pencil shelf marks and volume mark 亨 4, and the pencil note 'Li, Shih-chen, 1518-1593 / Pen ts'ao kang mu'. All three scans are the same image.
verdict.evidence: '# Expanded Compendium of Materia Medica' and 'Li Shizhen, 1518–1593' render the title and pencil note on page -184. The vocabulary table glosses and the trailing 'no date — no classification / Preface 4' are minor additions.

verdict.printed: Page 51 has only the title 銅發煩 (Bronze Bombard) and an illustration of a bombard on a wheeled carriage. There is no body text.
verdict.evidence: "It is cast from high-quality bronze to withstand the immense pressure of a heavy powder charge..." and "When the fuse is lit at the touch-hole... no armor or fortification can withstand its strike" are printed on no page. Page 50 is about Song-era cannons and page 52 is about weights and shot. The title is rendered, but the Volume 123 header and the term table are invented.
verdict.note: The English body is an invented essay and is not a rendering of any printed text.

verdict.printed: Page xiv of the Preface: the end of a sentence begun on the previous page, then the argument that moral books and Holy Books would have to be banned before this one, and the start of a sentence ending 'Il est à'.
verdict.evidence: 'The Holy Books, those of the Fathers, those of the Casuists, must all be prohibited before mine' renders the printed 'Les Livres Saints, ceux des Peres, ceux des Casuïstes doivent tous être prohibés avant le mien' on page 24.

verdict.printed: Greek text of Apollodorus III. xv. 8 (the Labyrinth, Daedalus, Talos), a critical apparatus, and English footnotes on Daedalus's parentage.
verdict.evidence: "in a labyrinth, from which it was impossible... Daedalus, the son of Eupalamus and Alcippe... threw Talos... off the Acropolis" renders the Greek "οὗτος ἐν λαβυρίνθῳ καθειργμένος... Δαίδαλος ὁ Εὐπαλάμου παῖς" printed on page 131. The apparatus and the English footnotes on page 131 are not rendered.

verdict.printed: Page 32 is body text only: the Novgorodians' treaty with Dimitriy, their seizure of Torzhok, Mikhail's assault, the defeat of Aleksandr Abakumovich, and the burning of the town. It also carries the margin notes 'Г. 1372.' and 'Маія 31.'.
verdict.evidence: "Mikhail's cavalry trampled their corpses, and the Prince... ordered the town set on fire from the far end with the wind" is printed on page 32. The English ends at "the monasteries and", matching the page's last line, and does not reach the 'churches, except three stone ones' text that opens page 33.

verdict.printed: Page 143 (printed 108): Journael entry for 12 July 1633. The ship runs aground on a sandbank off Texel, the cables break, and the crew and pilots despair. The page ends on 'gheen hope / om'.
verdict.evidence: "we ran aground on a sandbank, where our ship immediately sat dry by a good half foot" and "Friends, here there is entirely no hope", both printed on page 143. The English adds only a short gloss on Bewindhebbers, plus a summary and keywords that are metadata.

verdict.printed: Page 138 (printed 119, Libro XIV): the end of the sentence about the enemies, then the Casentino women and children lament fortune as they come to Florence. It has six footnotes, ending with the one on the particle 'che'.
verdict.evidence: "Therefore, because of the many adversities into which we had brought ourselves and our subjects" and "What <gloss>6</gloss>, must we endure the punishments of civic discord?" both render page 138. The only additions are a short summary and keywords, with a brief editorial gloss on 'Forse che' and 'grondeggiare'.

verdict.printed: Page 344 (header "Historie"): German body text saying the Bishop of Rome did nothing and the Emperor did everything in the Donatist disputes. It covers Miltiades as imperial commissioner, the absence of papal authority in African canon law, the Catholics' pride in the secular arm, Calvin and Balduin, and ends mid-sentence at "mit Unter-".
verdict.evidence: "the Bishop of Rome did nothing at all, while the Emperor did everything" and "Only once ... does Bishop Miltiades appear" are both printed on page 357. The summary and keywords are short additions. The "François Baudouin" gloss for Franz Balduin is a minor addition.

verdict.printed: Page 63, header 'De falsa relig.': Lactantius on Hercules serving Omphale, whether the poets can be believed, the Argonauts, Troy and Laomedon, and Hercules' madness. The text begins mid-sentence ('stabulo...') and breaks off at 'Philoctetes eius haeres non pu-'.
verdict.evidence: 'Hercules served not only King Eurystheus... but also the shameless woman Omphale' and 'But Philoctetes, his heir, did not think so' both come from page 63. The English begins at 'stable, than he who has cast out vices' and ends where page 63 ends.

verdict.printed: Page 131 (printed p. 120) has the Greek text of Apollodorus (οὗτος ἐν λαβυρίνθῳ καθειργμένος… Δαίδαλος… Τάλω), an apparatus criticus, and English notes on the Minotaur and Labyrinth and the parentage of Daedalus.
verdict.evidence: The stored English begins "When the war lingered on and he could not take Athens, he prayed to Zeus…" and ends "Now the Minotaur was confined...". That is the body text of page 130 (printed p. 119). Nothing from page 131's Greek, apparatus or notes is rendered. The added note on the Hyacinthides is a paraphrase of page 130's footnote, and the summary and keywords are extra.

verdict.printed: Page 1215 (printed 1138): the continuation of the entry on מקדש (sanctuary/palace), running from 'quit R.D. in lib. rad.' through Isaiah 8:14, 16:12, Psalm 74:7, Ezekiel 21:7 and Psalm 73:17, and ending at 'ubi finis est mercedis,'.
verdict.evidence: 'Because Shebna and his fellow conspirators made peace with the king of Assyria, but Hezekiah… refused' renders 'quia Sebná, & coniurati eius, fecerunt pacem cum rege Assúr…' (page 1215). The added glosses are minor: 'Rabbi David Kimchi', 'Aramaic paraphrase', and the English summary and keywords.

verdict.printed: Page 32: the continuation of the Novgorod–Tver conflict. It covers the Novgorod agreement with Dimitri, the seizure of Torzhok, the battle in which Alexander Abakumovich falls, and Mikhail burning the city. Page 31 carries the Kestutis raid on Pereslavl, Dmitrov and Kashin.
verdict.evidence: The English opens with 'did not wish to lead the army himself, but sent Kestutis, Vytautas...' and the Pereslavl and Kashin raid, all printed on page 31. It then renders page 32's 'the Novgorodians hastened to expel his governors' and 'the monasteries and'.
